prompt: Why is a load test run with jmeter -n rather than from the GUI?
hint: What else is using the processor while the GUI is open?

choices.text: The GUI cannot send HTTP requests
choices.why: It can; the GUI runs the same samplers, which is how a plan is debugged.

choices.text: Non-GUI mode sends requests over a faster protocol
choices.why: Both modes send the same HTTP; the difference is what else the process is doing.

choices.text: Drawing samples takes resources from the threads
choices.why: Right. The window competes with the virtual users, and the result partly measures the window.

choices.text: The GUI ignores the timers in the plan
choices.why: Timers run in both modes.

prompt: What is the JMeter GUI the right tool for?
hint: One or two users, and every response visible.

choices.text: Building a plan and debugging it with a user or two
choices.why: Right. Its listeners show each request and response, which is what debugging needs.

choices.text: Running the final load test so the graphs update live
choices.why: Live graphs during a load run take resources from the threads being measured.

choices.text: Starting the workers of a distributed test
choices.why: Workers run jmeter-server, which has no window.

choices.text: Measuring the system under test from inside the VM
choices.why: The VM has no desktop, so the GUI runs on your own computer.

prompt: Match each family of JMeter element to what it does.
hint: The table at the top of "A test plan, element by element".

pairs.right: the virtual users: how many, how fast, how long
sends one request and records one sample
sets up defaults, variables or data for the samplers
marks a sample failed when its response is wrong

right_distractors: sends the plan to the remote workers

prompt: The think timer sits at the thread group's level and runs before both samplers. Where would you put it so that only GET /shows/{id} waits?

choices.text: Under the test plan, above the thread group
choices.why: Higher in the tree widens the scope: it would apply to every sampler of every thread group.

choices.text: After the second sampler, at the same level
choices.why: Position among siblings does not narrow the scope; at that level it still applies to both.

choices.text: Inside the HTTP Request Defaults
choices.why: A config element is not a parent of the samplers, so nothing under it reaches them.

choices.text: Inside that sampler, beside the assertion
choices.why: Right. An element inside a sampler applies to that sampler alone.

prompt: What does the CSV Data Set Config in this plan do each time a thread needs a show?

choices.text: Gives every thread its own copy of the file to read from the top
choices.why: That is a per-thread share mode; shareMode.all makes the threads take turns at one file.

choices.text: Reads the next line of one shared file into show
choices.why: Right. Threads take turns, and at the end of the file it starts again from the top.

choices.text: Picks a random line of the file
choices.why: It reads in order; a random id would need a function such as __Random instead.

choices.text: Reads the whole file into one variable
choices.why: One line per use, into the variable named in variableNames.

prompt: The thread group reads its size with __P, so adding -J___=40 to the command runs forty threads.
Ten threads carry a Constant Throughput Timer set to 600 samples a minute, and the server slows until every sample takes 3 seconds. What rate does the test send?

choices.text: 600 a minute, because the timer holds the rate
choices.why: The timer can delay a thread, never speed it up; ten threads at 3 s each cannot reach ten a second.

choices.text: Near 200 a minute, all that ten 3 s loops allow
choices.why: Right. 10 / 3 s is about 3.3 a second. The test is still closed underneath.

choices.text: None, because the timer stops threads that fall behind
choices.why: It does not stop threads; it just has no waiting left to remove.

choices.text: 1,200 a minute, as the timer makes up the lost time
choices.why: There is no catching up in a closed model: a thread sends again only after its last answer.

prompt: What is the difference between a summary + line and a summary = line?
hint: One is a period, one is a total.

choices.text: + is for successes and = for the whole including errors
choices.why: Both lines count errors, in their Err column.

choices.text: + is the controller and = the workers
choices.why: Both appear in a run on one machine, with no workers at all.

choices.text: + is printed by the GUI and = by non-GUI mode
choices.why: Both are printed by the summariser in non-GUI mode.

choices.text: + covers the last period, = the run so far
choices.why: Right. The last = line is the whole run.

prompt: Twenty threads think for a uniform random 1 to 2 seconds before each request, and the responses take a few milliseconds. About how many requests a second should they send?
hint: Lesson 3: X = N / (R + Z), with Z the mean of the timer.

prompt: Why does a plan meant for load runs carry no listeners?
hint: What does View Results Tree keep?

choices.text: -l writes each sample to disk and holds none in memory
choices.why: Right. The .jtl is the listener for a load run, and everything else is built from it afterwards.

choices.text: Listeners are only allowed inside a sampler
choices.why: Listeners can sit at any level; scope decides which samples they hear.

choices.text: Listeners slow the server under test
choices.why: They run in the generator, and it is the generator they slow.

choices.text: Non-GUI mode refuses to load a plan that has one
choices.why: It loads them; they cost memory and processor time during the run.

prompt: JMeter already marks a 404 as a failed sample. What does the Response Assertion add?
hint: A server can answer 200 and still be wrong.

choices.text: It makes failed samples faster to record
choices.why: Assertions add checking work; they do not speed recording up.

choices.text: It retries the request when the status is wrong
choices.why: Assertions check; nothing in them sends a request again.

choices.text: It catches a 200 whose body is wrong
choices.why: Right. An empty list or an error page served as success passes the status check and fails the assertion.

choices.text: It counts the 404s separately from other errors
choices.why: All failed samples count as errors together; the message says which check failed.

prompt: In a line of the .jtl, what does the Latency column measure?

choices.text: The time spent opening the connection
choices.why: That is the Connect column.

choices.text: The time to the first byte of the answer
choices.why: Right. elapsed runs on to the last byte.

choices.text: The time the server reported in Server-Timing
choices.why: JMeter does not read that header; it times from the client.

choices.text: The wait the timer added before the request
choices.why: Timer delays are not part of a sample's time.

prompt: A distributed run uses -Jusers=10 on the controller, and the workers start twenty threads each. Why?
hint: Which machine does -J set a property on?

choices.text: The workers ignore properties of every kind
choices.why: They read properties sent with -G, and their own -J at start-up.

choices.text: Distributed mode doubles the users on purpose
choices.why: Each worker runs exactly what its properties say; nothing doubles.

choices.text: The ramp-up overrides the user count
choices.why: The ramp spreads the start of the threads; it does not set how many.

choices.text: -J stayed on the controller, so the default of 20 ran
choices.why: Right. -G sends a property to the workers; -J sets it only where it is typed.

prompt: A worker was started in a directory with no shows.csv. What happens when the controller starts the test?
hint: What travels from the controller, and what does not?

choices.text: It finds no data file and records no samples
choices.why: Right. The plan travels; the data file is read from the worker's own disk, and there was none.

choices.text: The controller sends its own copy of the file
choices.why: Only the plan and the -G properties are sent; files stay where they are.

choices.text: The worker downloads the file from the box office
choices.why: Nothing in JMeter fetches a data file over HTTP.

choices.text: The other worker's copy is shared over RMI
choices.why: Workers do not talk to each other, only to the controller.

prompt: jmeter-server refuses to start with "Cannot start. nft is a loopback address." What fixes it?
hint: Which address does the worker tell the controller?

choices.text: Turning off RMI encryption with server.rmi.ssl.disable
choices.why: Encryption is a separate setting; the message is about the address.

choices.text: Starting the worker as root with sudo
choices.why: Privilege does not change which address the hostname resolves to.

choices.text: Setting java.rmi.server.hostname to 127.0.0.1 or a real IP
choices.why: Right. The hostname resolved to 127.0.1.1, and this tells RMI which address to hand out instead.

choices.text: Choosing a server_port above 1099
choices.why: Any port gives the same error; it is the address that is refused.

prompt: The controller runs this lesson's plan with -R naming three workers and -Gusers=40. How many virtual users reach the box office?
hint: Each worker runs the whole plan.

prompt: Put the steps of a distributed JMeter run in order.
items: give each worker its own copy of the data file
run jmeter -n with -R and -G on the controller
the workers send their samples back to one .jtl
build the HTML report from the .jtl

prompt: Run from the GUI with View Results Tree open, 500 users give a 95th percentile of 900 ms. The same plan in non-GUI mode with -l gives 120 ms. Which describes the box office?
hint: Which run was also measuring JMeter?

choices.text: The GUI run, because it watched every response
choices.why: Watching every response is the cost: the window and the tree slowed the generator, and the times include that.

choices.text: The non-GUI run
choices.why: Right. With nothing held in memory and nothing drawn, the generator kept out of the measurement.

choices.text: Neither, as percentiles cannot compare two runs
choices.why: Two runs of the same plan can be compared by percentile; here one of them measured the tool.

choices.text: The mean of the two, about 510 ms
choices.why: Averaging a good measurement with a contaminated one gives a number that describes neither.
